3. Prop 1.6.4 (axiomatized in M6 as `beta_omega_strict` or derivable from the cd-index infrastructure).

**Case B (j < n-1 and j+1 ∉ D):** ω(D) and ω(D \ {j}) differ by swapping bit j for bit i = j-1 (not containment). This requires a more refined cd-index argument.

1	(* Layer 5: β-swap lemma and alternating-maximum corollary.                  *)
2	(*                                                                           *)
3	(* Proves that among descent sets D : {set 'I_n} which are not               *)
4	(* set-alternating (i.e. contain a consecutive same-membership pair),        *)
5	(* β(D) is strictly smaller than β(alt_desc_set n).                          *)
6	(*                                                                           *)
7	(* Two LABELED ADMITTED sub-lemmas remain: `beta_swap_monotone`              *)
8	(* (Foata injection) and `beta_swap_lt` (strict witness). Everything         *)
9	(* downstream — `beta_alt_max` — is `Qed`.                                  *)

11	From mathcomp Require Import all_ssreflect fingroup perm.
12	From mathcomp_eulerian Require Import
13	  ordinal_reindex perm_compress descent eulerian beta.
14	
15	Set Implicit Arguments.
16	Unset Strict Implicit.
17	Unset Printing Implicit Defensive.
18	
19	(* ========================================================================= *)
20	(* §A. Symmetric difference and single-position toggle                       *)
21	(* ========================================================================= *)
22	
23	Definition sym_diff (n : nat) (D E : {set 'I_n}) : {set 'I_n} :=
24	  (D :\: E) :|: (E :\: D).
25	
26	Definition toggle_at (n : nat) (D : {set 'I_n}) (i : 'I_n) : {set 'I_n} :=
27	  sym_diff D [set i].
28	
29	Lemma toggle_at_in n (D : {set 'I_n}) (i j : 'I_n) :
30	  (j \in toggle_at D i) = (i == j) (+) (j \in D).
31	Proof.
32	rewrite /toggle_at /sym_diff !inE eq_sym.
33	by case: eqP => _ /=; case: (j \in D).
34	Qed.
35	
36	Lemma toggle_atK n (D : {set 'I_n}) (i : 'I_n) :
37	  toggle_at (toggle_at D i) i = D.
38	Proof.
39	apply/setP => j; rewrite !toggle_at_in.
40	by case: eqP => _ /=; case: (j \in D).
41	Qed.
42	
43	Lemma toggle_at_self n (D : {set 'I_n}) (i : 'I_n) :
44	  (i \in toggle_at D i) = ~~ (i \in D).
45	Proof. by rewrite toggle_at_in eqxx. Qed.
46	
47	Lemma toggle_at_other n (D : {set 'I_n}) (i j : 'I_n) :
48	  i != j -> (j \in toggle_at D i) = (j \in D).
49	Proof. by move=> H; rewrite toggle_at_in (negbTE H). Qed.
50	
51	(* ========================================================================= *)
52	(* §B. Alternating descent set                                               *)
53	(* ========================================================================= *)
54	
55	Definition alt_desc_set (n : nat) : {set 'I_n} :=
56	  [set i : 'I_n | ~~ odd i].
57	
58	Lemma mem_alt_desc_set n (i : 'I_n) :
59	  (i \in alt_desc_set n) = ~~ odd i.
60	Proof. by rewrite inE. Qed.
61	
62	(* A descent set is "set-alternating" iff every consecutive pair has
63	   differing membership. *)
64	Definition set_is_alt (n : nat) (D : {set 'I_n}) : bool :=
65	  [forall i : 'I_n, [forall j : 'I_n,
66	     (val j == (val i).+1) ==> ((i \in D) != (j \in D))]].
67	
68	(* The alternating set is set-alternating. *)
69	Lemma alt_desc_set_is_alt n : set_is_alt (alt_desc_set n).
70	Proof.
71	apply/forallP => i; apply/forallP => j; apply/implyP => /eqP Hj.
72	rewrite !mem_alt_desc_set Hj /= negbK.
73	by case: (odd i).
74	Qed.
75	
76	Lemma set_not_altP n (D : {set 'I_n}) :
77	  ~~ set_is_alt D ->
78	  exists i j : 'I_n, val j = (val i).+1 /\ (i \in D) = (j \in D).
79	Proof.
80	move/forallPn => [i /forallPn [j Hij]].
81	rewrite negb_imply in Hij.
82	case/andP: Hij => /eqP Hj /negPn /eqP Heq.
83	by exists i, j.
84	Qed.
85	
86	(* ========================================================================= *)
87	(* §C. β-swap lemmas (Foata — classical)                                      *)
88	(* ========================================================================= *)
89	
90	(* The following axioms are a special case of a classical theorem:
91	
92	     Stanley, Enumerative Combinatorics Vol. 1 (2nd ed.), Proposition 1.6.4.
93	     If ω(S) ⊂ ω(T), then βₙ(S) < βₙ(T).
94	
95	   (The ω-map of §1.6 sends S ⊆ [n-1] to the subset of i ∈ [n-2] for which
96	   exactly one of i, i+1 lies in S.) When i, j = i+1 are both descents of D,
97	   toggling i flips at least the ω-bit at position i, extending ω(D); this
98	   is the strict-extension case of 1.6.4 (see §H below for the partial
99	   ω-bridge already formalized).
100

100	
101	   Stanley's proof of 1.6.4 is non-trivial: it routes through the cd-index
102	   of §1.6.3 (Theorem 1.6.3, "the ab-index Ψₙ can be written as a polynomial
103	   in c = a+b and d = ab+ba with nonnegative integer coefficients"), which
104	   in turn requires the min-max-tree machinery (Facts #1–#3) including the
105	   commuting ψᵢ involutions and their descent-set effect.
106	
107	   No shorter self-contained combinatorial argument is known to us. Naïve
108	   rotation-based bijections fail at block-boundary cases (an explicit S₉
109	   counterexample is documented in AXIOMS_TODO.md). Formalizing 1.6.4
110	   end-to-end is estimated at 3–5 weeks of MathComp development; see
111	   AXIOMS_TODO.md for the preserved partial infrastructure (omega_set in
112	   §H, Foata block endpoints in §I) and a roadmap for a future attempt.
113	
114	   We axiomatize only the "both descents" case (both i, j = i+1 ∈ D). The
115	   "both ascents" case is DERIVED from this axiom via the value-complement
116	   involution (compl_perm, beta_compl, descent_set_compl), reducing the
117	   axiomatic content to one case. *)
118	
119	(* "Both descents" monotonicity (atomic axiom).
120	   NOTE: toggles the UPPER index j = i+1, not i. Toggling the lower index
121	   can decrease β — counterexample: n=4, D={2,3}, i=2, β(D)=6 > 4=β(D\{2}).
122	   Toggling j removes the upper descent, which always increases β. *)
123	Axiom beta_swap_monotone_both_in : forall n (D : {set 'I_n}) (i j : 'I_n),
124	  val j = (val i).+1 ->
125	  i \in D -> j \in D ->
126	  beta D <= beta (toggle_at D j).
127	
128	(* "Both descents" strict version (atomic axiom). *)
129	Axiom beta_swap_lt_both_in : forall n (D : {set 'I_n}) (i j : 'I_n),
130	  val j = (val i).+1 ->
131	  i \in D -> j \in D ->
132	  beta D < beta (toggle_at D j).
133	
134	(* Toggle commutes with complement on the set side.
135	   Used to reduce the "both ascents" case to the "both descents" case. *)
136	Lemma toggle_at_compl n (D : {set 'I_n}) (i : 'I_n) :
137	  toggle_at (~: D) i = ~: toggle_at D i.
138	Proof.
139	apply/setP => j.
140	have H1 : (j \in toggle_at (~: D) i) = (i == j) (+) ~~ (j \in D).
141	  by rewrite toggle_at_in inE.
142	have H2 : (j \in ~: toggle_at D i) = ~~ ((i == j) (+) (j \in D)).
143	  by rewrite inE toggle_at_in.
144	rewrite H1 H2.
145	by case: (i == j); case: (j \in D).
146	Qed.
147	
148	(* β-swap monotonicity and strict version are derived (via complement
149	   reduction) further below, after the value-complement bijection is
150	   available (§E). *)
151	
152	(* ========================================================================= *)
153	(* §D. Alt maximises β (deferred: depends on derived beta_swap_lt below)     *)
154	(* ========================================================================= *)
155	
156	(* We measure distance from alt by Hamming distance (symmetric-difference
157	   cardinality). The key observation: if D has a consecutive same-type
158	   pair (i, j), then at least one of i, j disagrees with alt_desc_set;
159	   toggling at that position reduces the Hamming distance to alt by 1.
160	
161	   Proof: a pair (i, j) at positions val i, val i + 1 has same D-membership.
162	   But alt_desc_set has different membership at i vs j (since parities
163	   differ). So if D agrees with alt at i, it must disagree at j (and vice
164	   versa). In either case, at least one of {i, j} disagrees with alt. We
165	   toggle at the disagreeing position — it enters alt, so Hamming distance
166	   drops by 1 (while the symmetry of the pair guarantees the other swap
167	   hypothesis still holds at that position). *)
168	
169	Lemma alt_pair_parity n (i j : 'I_n) :
170	  val j = (val i).+1 -> (i \in alt_desc_set n) != (j \in alt_desc_set n).
171	Proof.
172	move=> Hj.
173	rewrite !mem_alt_desc_set Hj /= negbK.
174	by case: (odd i).
175	Qed.
176	
177	(* Toggling at k where k ∈ sym_diff D alt reduces the Hamming distance. *)
178	Lemma sym_diff_toggle_in n (D : {set 'I_n}) (k : 'I_n) :
179	  k \in sym_diff D (alt_desc_set n) ->
180	  #|sym_diff (toggle_at D k) (alt_desc_set n)|
181	    < #|sym_diff D (alt_desc_set n)|.
182	Proof.
183	move=> Hk.
184	rewrite (cardsD1 k (sym_diff D (alt_desc_set n))) Hk add1n ltnS.
185	apply: subset_leq_card; apply/subsetP => x.
186	rewrite inE !in_setD [x \in toggle_at D k]toggle_at_in.
187	rewrite /sym_diff !inE.
188	case E : (k == x) => /=.
189	- move/eqP: E => Ekx; subst x.
190	  rewrite eqxx.
191	  move: Hk; rewrite /sym_diff !inE.
192	  by case: (k \in D); case: (odd k).
193	- rewrite eq_sym E /=.
194	  by case: (x \in D); case: (odd x).
195	Qed.
196	
197	(* Symmetric difference is empty iff the sets are equal. *)
198	Lemma sym_diff_eq0 n (D E : {set 'I_n}) :
199	  #|sym_diff D E| = 0 -> D = E.

200	Proof.
201	move=> /eqP; rewrite cards_eq0 => /eqP Hsd.
202	apply/setP => j.
203	have : j \notin sym_diff D E by rewrite Hsd inE.
204	rewrite /sym_diff !inE negb_or !negb_and !negbK.
205	case/andP => H1 H2; apply/idP/idP => H.
206	- case/orP: H1 => //; by rewrite H.
207	- case/orP: H2 => //; by rewrite H.
208	Qed.
209	
210	(* ========================================================================= *)
211	(* §E. Value-complement bijection                                             *)
212	(* ========================================================================= *)
213	
214	(* The "value-complement" perm: replace every value v by rev_ord v.
215	   Effect on descents: every descent becomes ascent and vice versa.
216	   This is the second symmetry (along with rev_perm) needed to identify
217	   the two set-alternating descent sets. *)
218	Definition compl_perm n (s : {perm 'I_n.+1}) : {perm 'I_n.+1} :=
219	  s * rev_perm_ord n.
220	
221	Lemma compl_permE n (s : {perm 'I_n.+1}) (i : 'I_n.+1) :
222	  compl_perm s i = rev_ord (s i).
223	Proof. by rewrite /compl_perm permM rev_perm_ordE. Qed.
224	
225	Lemma compl_perm_inj n : injective (@compl_perm n).
226	Proof. by move=> s1 s2 H; apply: (mulIg (rev_perm_ord n)). Qed.
227	
228	Lemma compl_perm_involutive n : involutive (@compl_perm n).
229	Proof.
230	move=> s; rewrite /compl_perm -mulgA.
231	have -> : (rev_perm_ord n * rev_perm_ord n)%g = 1%g.
232	  apply/permP => i; rewrite permM perm1 !rev_perm_ordE.
233	  exact: rev_ordK.
234	by rewrite mulg1.
235	Qed.
236	
237	Lemma is_descent_compl n (s : {perm 'I_n.+1}) (i : 'I_n) :
238	  is_descent (compl_perm s) i = ~~ is_descent s i.
239	Proof.
240	rewrite /is_descent !compl_permE.
241	set a := s _; set b := s _.
242	have arg_ne : widen_ord (leqnSn n) i != lift ord0 i.
243	  by rewrite -val_eqE /= /bump /= add1n neq_ltn ltnSn.
244	have ab_ne : val a != val b.
245	  by rewrite val_eqE; apply: contra arg_ne; rewrite /a /b => /eqP /perm_inj ->.
246	rewrite /= ltn_sub2lE; last exact: ltn_ord.
247	by rewrite ltnS ltn_neqAle [_ == _]eq_sym ab_ne /= -leqNgt.
248	Qed.
249	
250	Lemma descent_set_compl n (s : {perm 'I_n.+1}) :
251	  descent_set (compl_perm s) = ~: descent_set s.
252	Proof.
253	by apply/setP => i; rewrite !inE is_descent_compl.
254	Qed.
255	
256	Lemma beta_compl n (D : {set 'I_n}) : beta D = beta (~: D).
257	Proof.
258	rewrite /beta.
259	rewrite -(card_imset _ (@compl_perm_inj n)).
260	congr #|pred_of_set _|; apply/setP => s; rewrite !inE.
261	apply/imsetP/idP.
262	- by case=> t; rewrite inE => /eqP <- ->; rewrite descent_set_compl.
263	- move=> /eqP Hs.
264	  exists (compl_perm s); last by rewrite compl_perm_involutive.
265	  by rewrite inE descent_set_compl Hs setCK.
266	Qed.
267	
268	(* β-swap monotonicity: if positions i and j = i+1 have the same
269	   D-membership, then toggling j does not decrease β. Derived from the
270	   "both descents" axiom `beta_swap_monotone_both_in` via the value-
271	   complement involution: when both i, j are ASCENTS in D, they are both
272	   DESCENTS in ~: D; applying the axiom to ~: D and translating back via
273	   `beta_compl` yields the inequality for D. *)
274	Lemma beta_swap_monotone n (D : {set 'I_n}) (i j : 'I_n) :
275	  val j = (val i).+1 ->
276	  (i \in D) = (j \in D) ->
277	  beta D <= beta (toggle_at D j).
278	Proof.
279	move=> Hj Hij.
280	case Hi : (i \in D).
281	- have Hj' : j \in D by rewrite -Hij.
282	  exact: (beta_swap_monotone_both_in Hj Hi Hj').
283	- have Hi' : i \in ~: D by rewrite !inE Hi.
284	  have Hj' : j \in ~: D by rewrite !inE -Hij Hi.
285	  have H := beta_swap_monotone_both_in Hj Hi' Hj'.
286	  rewrite toggle_at_compl in H.
287	  by rewrite (beta_compl D) (beta_compl (toggle_at D j)).
288	Qed.
289	
290	(* Strict version, derived identically. *)
291	Lemma beta_swap_lt n (D : {set 'I_n}) (i j : 'I_n) :
292	  val j = (val i).+1 ->
293	  (i \in D) = (j \in D) ->
294	  beta D < beta (toggle_at D j).
295	Proof.
296	move=> Hj Hij.
297	case Hi : (i \in D).
298	- have Hj' : j \in D by rewrite -Hij.
299	  exact: (beta_swap_lt_both_in Hj Hi Hj').

300	- have Hi' : i \in ~: D by rewrite !inE Hi.
301	  have Hj' : j \in ~: D by rewrite !inE -Hij Hi.
302	  have H := beta_swap_lt_both_in Hj Hi' Hj'.
303	  rewrite toggle_at_compl in H.
304	  by rewrite (beta_compl D) (beta_compl (toggle_at D j)).
305	Qed.
306	
307	(* ========================================================================= *)
308	(* §F. Classification of set-alternating sets                                *)
309	(* ========================================================================= *)
310	
311	(* A set_is_alt set on 'I_n is determined by its membership at 0:
312	   either alt_desc_set (= even positions) or its complement (= odd). *)
313	
314	Lemma set_is_alt_classify n (D : {set 'I_n}) :
315	  set_is_alt D -> D = alt_desc_set n \/ D = ~: alt_desc_set n.
316	Proof.
317	move=> HD.
318	case: n D HD => [|n] D HD.
319	  by left; apply/setP; case; case.
320	have HD' : forall (i1 i2 : 'I_n.+1), val i2 = (val i1).+1 ->
321	  (i1 \in D) != (i2 \in D).
322	  move=> i1 i2 Hi12.
323	  have := forallP (forallP HD i1) i2.
324	  by rewrite Hi12 eqxx.
325	have helper : forall v (i : 'I_n.+1), val i = v ->
326	  (i \in D) = (ord0 \in D) (+) odd v.
327	  elim/ltn_ind => v IHv i Hv.
328	  case: v IHv Hv => [|v] IHv Hv.
329	  - have -> : i = ord0 by apply/val_inj.
330	    by rewrite addbF.
331	  - have Hvn : v < n.+1 by rewrite -Hv; apply: ltnW; exact: ltn_ord.
332	    have IHv' : (Ordinal Hvn \in D) = (ord0 \in D) (+) odd v.
333	      by apply: (IHv v (ltnSn v) (Ordinal Hvn) erefl).
334	    have Halt : val i = (val (Ordinal Hvn)).+1 by rewrite Hv.
335	    have := HD' (Ordinal Hvn) i Halt.
336	    rewrite IHv' /=.
337	    by case: (ord0 \in D); case: (i \in D); case: (odd v).
338	case Hord0 : (ord0 \in D).
339	- left; apply/setP => i.
340	  rewrite mem_alt_desc_set (helper (val i) i erefl) Hord0 /=.
341	  by case: (odd i).
342	- right; apply/setP => i.
343	  rewrite inE mem_alt_desc_set (helper (val i) i erefl) Hord0 /=.
344	  by case: (odd i).
345	Qed.
346	
347	(* Helper for the second-alt branch: if D' is set_is_alt then β(D') = β(alt). *)
348	Lemma beta_set_is_alt_eq n (D' : {set 'I_n}) :
349	  set_is_alt D' -> beta D' = beta (alt_desc_set n).
350	Proof.
351	move=> /set_is_alt_classify [-> //|->].
352	by rewrite beta_compl setCK.
353	Qed.
354	
355	(* ========================================================================= *)
356	(* §G. β-based induction driver                                              *)
357	(* ========================================================================= *)
358	
359	(* The right well-founded measure is `n.+1`! - β D` (decreases under
360	   beta_swap_lt because β strictly increases). The original `find_reducing_toggle`
361	   used Hamming distance to alt, which is NOT monotone under beta_swap_lt
362	   — see counter-example D = {0, 2, 3} on 'I_4 where the only same-pair
363	   toggle increases the Hamming distance but β does increase. *)
364	
365	(* From ~~set_is_alt D, the existence of a same-pair forces n ≥ 2;
366	   hence [set: 'I_n] and set0 are distinct, both have β ≥ 1, so β D < n.+1`!. *)
367	Lemma not_set_is_alt_n_ge2 n (D : {set 'I_n}) :
368	  ~~ set_is_alt D -> 1 < n.
369	Proof.

432	(* Stanley EC1 §1.6, Prop. 1.6.4: for S ⊆ [n-1], define ω(S) ⊆ [n-2] by
433	   "i ∈ ω(S) iff exactly one of i, i+1 lies in S". We encode ω-maps as
434	   functions {set 'I_n.+1} → {set 'I_n} (aligning with how `beta` sees
435	   descent-sets for perms of 'I_n.+2 — the +1 shift matches Stanley's
436	   "[n-2]" vs "[n-1]"). The target β-axioms in §C use descent-sets of type
437	   {set 'I_n} (no .+1); callers bridge via the obvious `Ordinal` packaging.
438	
439	   NOTE ON THE PLAN: STANLEY_CDINDEX_PLAN.md §2 asserts that toggling any
440	   "both-in-D" descent gives a strict ω-superset. Direct case-analysis
441	   (mirrored in the proof below) shows this is TOO STRONG: toggling `i` also
442	   flips the ω-bit at `i-1`, and that bit LEAVES ω(D) precisely when
443	   (i-1) ∉ D. A concrete counterexample: D = {1,2} ⊆ 'I_3, i = 1:
444	     ω(D) = {0}, ω(toggle D 1) = ω({2}) = {1}; neither contains the other.
445	   The strict-superset statement is therefore accurate only under the extra
446	   hypothesis that `i-1 ∈ D` (Case A of the flip analysis) OR that `i = 0`
447	   (no predecessor bit to flip). We expose both the strong, correctly
448	   hypothesised bridge (`toggle_at_omega_strict_superset`) and the always-
449	   true "new bit" lemma (`toggle_at_omega_bit_i_new`). Closing the axioms
450	   of §C via the bridge will therefore require either the full Stanley
451	   cd-index nonneg theorem (M5/M6 of the plan) or a case split on
452	   `(i-1) ∈ D` combined with an auxiliary argument for Case B.                  *)

454	Definition omega_set (n : nat) (D : {set 'I_n.+1}) : {set 'I_n} :=
455	  [set k : 'I_n | (widen_ord (leqnSn n) k \in D) != (lift ord0 k \in D)].

457	Lemma mem_omega_set n (D : {set 'I_n.+1}) (k : 'I_n) :
458	  (k \in omega_set D) =
459	  ((widen_ord (leqnSn n) k \in D) != (lift ord0 k \in D)).
460	Proof. by rewrite inE. Qed.

463	Lemma toggle_at_omega_bit_i_new n (D : {set 'I_n.+1}) (i j : 'I_n.+1) :
464	  val j = (val i).+1 -> i \in D -> j \in D ->
465	  exists k : 'I_n,
466	    [/\ widen_ord (leqnSn n) k = i,
467	        lift ord0 k = j,
468	        k \notin omega_set D &
469	        k \in omega_set (toggle_at D i)].

472	have Hik : val i < n.

474	pose k := Ordinal Hik.

480	by rewrite mem_omega_set Ewid Elif toggle_at_self Hi /= toggle_at_other // Hj'.

542	Definition left_ok s i (l : 'I_n) : bool :=
543	  (val l <= val i)

546	(* Predicate: every position in [val i, val r] is a descent. *)
547	Definition right_ok s i (r : 'I_n) : bool :=
548	  (val i <= val r)
549	  && [forall k : 'I_n, (val i <= val k <= val r) ==> is_descent s k].

552	Proof.
553	move=> Hi; rewrite /left_ok leqnn /=.
554	apply/forallP => k; apply/implyP; case/andP => H1 H2.

568	Definition block_left s i : 'I_n :=

570	  else i.

573	  if is_descent s i then [arg max_(r > i | right_ok s i r) val r]

618	Lemma block_left_descent s i (k : 'I_n) :
619	  is_descent s i ->

621	Proof.

628	  val i <= val k <= val (block_right s i) -> is_descent s k.

634	(* Combined: every position in [block_left, block_right] is a descent. *)
635	Lemma block_descent_chain s i (k : 'I_n) :
636	  is_descent s i ->
637	  val (block_left s i) <= val k <= val (block_right s i) ->
638	  is_descent s k.

640	move=> Hi Hk; case/andP: Hk => H1 H2.

681	Lemma block_right_maximal s i :

683	  forall r' : 'I_n, val r' = (val (block_right s i)).+1 ->
684	  ~~ is_descent s r'.

1	# Milestone 7: Closing the two axioms in `beta_swap.v`
2	
3	**Critical finding:** The two axioms as currently stated are **false**. The
4	toggle direction is wrong: the axioms toggle at i (the lower of two
5	consecutive descents), but should toggle at j = i+1 (the upper one).
6	This note documents the counterexamples, diagnoses the root cause, explains
7	why the naive omega-bridge approach fails, and provides the corrected
8	axiom statements with a proof outline.
9	
10	---
11	
12	## 1. The two axioms --- precise statement
13	
14	In `beta_swap.v` (lines 119--129), the two axioms are:
15	
16	```coq
17	Axiom beta_swap_monotone_both_in : forall n (D : {set 'I_n}) (i j : 'I_n),
18	  val j = (val i).+1 -> i \in D -> j \in D ->
19	  beta D <= beta (toggle_at D i).
20	
21	Axiom beta_swap_lt_both_in : forall n (D : {set 'I_n}) (i j : 'I_n),
22	  val j = (val i).+1 -> i \in D -> j \in D ->
23	  beta D < beta (toggle_at D i).
24	```
25	
26	**Mathematical translation.** Fix n >= 1. Let D be a subset of
27	{0, 1, ..., n-1} (encoded as `{set 'I_n}`). Define
28	
29	    beta(D) = |{sigma in S_{n+1} : descent_set(sigma) = D}|.
30	
31	When both i and j = i+1 are in D, `toggle_at D i = D Delta {i}`. Since
32	i is in D, this gives D \ {i}. The axioms claim beta(D) <= beta(D \ {i})
33	(weak) and beta(D) < beta(D \ {i}) (strict).
34	
35	---
36	
37	## 2. The axioms are false: counterexamples
38	
39	### 2.1 Strict axiom fails: n = 3, D = {1,2}, i = 1
40	
41	Permutations of {0,1,2,3} = S_4. We take i = 1, j = 2, both in D.
42	toggle_at({1,2}, 1) = {2}.
43	
44	**beta({1,2}) --- descent set {1,2}: sigma(0) < sigma(1) > sigma(2) > sigma(3).**
45	
46	sigma(1) must be the maximum of the last three values and sigma(0) < sigma(1).
47	
48	- sigma(1) = 3: sigma(0) in {0,1,2}; sigma(2) > sigma(3) from remaining.
49	  - sigma(0)=0: (sigma(2),sigma(3)) = (2,1). Perm (0,3,2,1). D = {1,2}. Good.
50	  - sigma(0)=1: (sigma(2),sigma(3)) = (2,0). Perm (1,3,2,0). D = {1,2}. Good.
51	  - sigma(0)=2: (sigma(2),sigma(3)) = (1,0). Perm (2,3,1,0). D = {1,2}. Good.
52	
53	No other value of sigma(1) works (checked: sigma(1) = 2 leads to remaining
54	values that can't satisfy both constraints). **beta({1,2}) = 3.**
55	
56	**beta({2}) --- descent set {2}: sigma(0) < sigma(1) < sigma(2) > sigma(3).**
57	
58	- sigma(2) = 3: sigma(0) < sigma(1) from {0,1,2}, sigma(3) = remaining.
59	  - (0,1,3,2), (0,2,3,1), (1,2,3,0). All have D = {2}. 3 perms.
60	
61	No other sigma(2) works. **beta({2}) = 3.**
62	
63	**Result: beta({1,2}) = 3 = beta({2}). The strict axiom claims 3 < 3. FALSE.**
64	
65	### 2.2 Both axioms fail: n = 4, D = {2,3}, i = 2
66	
67	Permutations of {0,1,2,3,4} = S_5. i = 2, j = 3, both in D.
68	toggle_at({2,3}, 2) = {3}.
69	
70	**beta({2,3}) --- sigma(0) < sigma(1) < sigma(2) > sigma(3) > sigma(4).**
71	
72	sigma(2) = 4: left pair from {0,1,2,3} (C(4,2) = 6 ways), right pair in
73	decreasing order from remaining. All 6 are valid:
74	(0,1,4,3,2), (0,2,4,3,1), (0,3,4,2,1), (1,2,4,3,0), (1,3,4,2,0), (2,3,4,1,0).
75	
76	sigma(2) <= 3 gives no valid perms (remaining values always include 4
77	which can't be placed in a decreasing sequence below sigma(2)).
78	**beta({2,3}) = 6.**
79	
80	**beta({3}) --- sigma(0) < sigma(1) < sigma(2) < sigma(3) > sigma(4).**
81	
82	sigma(3) = 4: first three values increasing from {0,1,2,3}, last value =
83	remaining. C(4,3) = 4 ways:
84	(0,1,2,4,3), (0,1,3,4,2), (0,2,3,4,1), (1,2,3,4,0).
85	
86	sigma(3) <= 3: remaining values include 4 which must go before sigma(3)
87	but then sigma(2) < sigma(3) <= 3 < 4 = sigma(earlier) breaks the
88	increasing condition. No valid perms. **beta({3}) = 4.**
89	
90	**Result: beta({2,3}) = 6, beta({3}) = 4. The monotone axiom claims
91	6 <= 4. FALSE. The strict axiom claims 6 < 4. FALSE.**

93	### 2.3 The correct direction: toggle at j
94	
95	With the same setup but toggling j instead of i:
96	
97	**n = 3, D = {1,2}, toggle at j = 2:** toggle_at({1,2}, 2) = {1}.
98	beta({1}) --- sigma(0) < sigma(1) > sigma(2) < sigma(3):
99	- sigma(1) = 3: 3 perms (vary sigma(0)).
100	- sigma(1) = 2: 2 perms.

100	- sigma(1) = 2: 2 perms.
101	Total: **beta({1}) = 5.** Inequality: 3 < 5. TRUE.
102	
103	**n = 4, D = {2,3}, toggle at j = 3:** toggle_at({2,3}, 3) = {2}.

## Report

### What was done

Replaced the two `Axiom` declarations (`beta_swap_monotone_both_in` and `beta_swap_lt_both_in`) in `/scratch/lelarge/mathcomp-eulerian/beta_swap.v` with `Lemma` + `Proof` + `Qed`, and added supporting infrastructure.

### Axioms converted to lemmas

- **`beta_swap_lt_both_in`** (strict version, `<`): Now a `Lemma`, proved by case-splitting on whether there exists `q : 'I_n` with `val q = (val j).+1` and `q \notin D`. Case A dispatches to `beta_swap_lt_caseA`; Case B dispatches to `beta_swap_lt_caseB`.

- **`beta_swap_monotone_both_in`** (weak version, `<=`): Now a `Lemma`, proved trivially from the strict version via `ltnW`.

### New axioms introduced (2)

1. **`beta_swap_lt_caseA`**: When `j` is at the boundary or `j+1 \in D` (i.e., `forall q, val q = (val j).+1 -> q \in D`), `beta D < beta (toggle_at D j)`. Justified by `toggle_at_j_omega_strict_superset` (proved below) + Prop 1.6.4 (seq-level in `psi.v`). The remaining gap is the finset/seq type bridge.

2. **`beta_swap_lt_caseB`**: When `j+1 \notin D` (i.e., `exists q, val q = (val j).+1 /\ q \notin D`), `beta D < beta (toggle_at D j)`. Justified by cd-index marginal-contribution comparison (requires Theorem 1.6.3 + monotonicity on min-max tree structure).

### New proved lemmas (2)

Added in Section H as j-toggle analogues of the existing i-toggle omega lemmas:

1. **`toggle_at_j_omega_bit_i_new`**: Toggling `j` always creates a new omega-bit at position `i`. (Fully proved, ~15 LOC.)

2. **`toggle_at_j_omega_strict_superset`**: Under the Case A hypothesis, `omega_set D \proper omega_set (toggle_at D j)`. (Fully proved, ~35 LOC.)

### Print Assumptions output

- **`beta_swap_monotone_both_in`**: depends on `beta_swap_lt_caseA`, `beta_swap_lt_caseB`
- **`beta_swap_lt_both_in`**: depends on `beta_swap_lt_caseA`, `beta_swap_lt_caseB`
- **`beta_alt_max`**: depends on `beta_swap_lt_caseA`, `beta_swap_lt_caseB`

### LOC

- 100 net lines added (798 -> 898)
- ~30 lines of new comments/documentation
- ~70 lines of new proved code + axiom declarations
